## Constraints

- Keep working until everything the brief asks for is done, and only stop to ask when you can't go on without the coordinator or before a risky step. If you must stop, hand back blocked and say why.
- Real-check rule: report a change done only with the output of a real check that exercises it (tests, type-checker, build, the changed command, or for infrastructure a plan or dry run against the target); a syntax-only check, or a check that failed to start, does not count. Install declared dependencies only with the project's own package manager and lockfile, never with sudo or the system package manager. If no real check can run, name the check not run and why.

- Merge rules: a review of record binds only to the exact head it reviewed, so any change to the head, including an update-branch, needs a delta review posted before merging; every merge must run the merge guard in `references/code-review.md` and carry the reviewed full head SHA as the expected-head condition (on GitHub, `gh pr merge <n> --match-head-commit <full reviewed SHA>`).

- Secrets rule: never write secrets to files or argv.
- Shell rule: run each shell step as one simple command with literal values; never assign a variable and use it in the same command; never feed a `$(...)` result into a later argument of the same command; and never prefix a command with an inline `VAR="$SECRET"` assignment - rely on the credential the session environment or the tool's own credential configuration already provides.
